Alliteration Marker

Paste a poem and the tool breaks it into syllables, tags each syllable's sound and stress using the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (built into this file, so it works offline), and renders the alliterative pattern back onto the original text with colored boxes.

Sound chart

1 · Paste the poem

Separate stanzas with a blank line, exactly as in the source text.

2 · Check the syllables, sounds, and stress

Syllables, sounds, and stress come from the dictionary, so they are usually right — but check them. Words outlined in gold are not in the dictionary and were guessed from their spelling. Click a syllable's text to fix a split (✂ split / ⤙ merge). The first dropdown is the sound the syllable starts with; the second is the sound it ends with. The circle toggles stressed (filled) / unstressed (empty). One-syllable words and syllables with only secondary stress in the dictionary are the ones to check against the poem's meter. A ↻ button means the dictionary lists more than one pronunciation for that word.

3 · Marked-up poem

Solid box = the sound falls on a stressed syllable. Dashed box = unstressed. Box color follows the chart above.

Pronunciations: The CMU Pronouncing Dictionary, Copyright © 1993–2015 Carnegie Mellon University. Syllable boundaries and letter-to-sound matching are computed by this tool and can be wrong — treat every chip as a draft to correct.
